questions_for_doctor: Are there any specific lifestyle adjustments I should consider to maintain these healthy blood parameters?
How often should I have a CBC test done as part of my routine health monitoring?
Are there any other preventative screenings or tests you would recommend based on my age and overall health?

recommended_foods: Lean proteins (e.g., chicken, fish, beans, lentils) for overall cell health.
Whole grains (e.g., oats, brown rice, quinoa) for sustained energy and fiber.
A variety of fruits and vegetables (e.g., berries, leafy greens, bell peppers) for antioxidants and vitamins.
Healthy fats (e.g., avocados, nuts, seeds, olive oil) for essential fatty acids.
Dairy or fortified plant-based alternatives for calcium and vitamin D.
foods_to_avoid: Excessive intake of highly processed foods high in unhealthy fats and sugars.
Large amounts of artificial sweeteners and additives.
Excessive alcohol consumption, which can impact overall health.
hydration_and_habits: Drink adequate water throughout the day to support blood volume and overall bodily functions.
Engage in regular physical activity, such as walking or cycling, to promote circulation and cardiovascular health.
Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep per night to support cellular repair and regeneration.
key_nutrients: Iron (essential for hemoglobin production and oxygen transport)
Vitamin B12 (crucial for red blood cell formation and neurological function)
Folate (important for DNA synthesis and cell division, including blood cells)
Vitamin C (enhances iron absorption and acts as an antioxidant)
